proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences, divisibility of central binomial coefficients, and pairing the terms indexed by \(k\) and \(p+k\) show that both sequences vanish modulo \(p\) from indices \(p\) through \(2p-2\), while at index \(p-1\) their values are respectively \(1\) and \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Thus each Hankel matrix is anti-triangular modulo \(p\), so only the reversal permutation survives in the determinant expansion; its sign is \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\), and the constant antidiagonal products give the two claimed residues (with the second sign product cancelling to \(1\)).
